Tabulate missing values

Source: R/misstable.R
misstable.Rd

Missing-value summaries, like Stata's misstable.

  • By default, misstable() counts the missing values of each variable, like misstable summarize.

  • With .patterns = TRUE, it counts the combinations of observed and missing variables across rows, like misstable patterns.

Usage

misstable(.data, ..., .by = NULL, .patterns = FALSE, .all = FALSE)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

<tidy-select> Variables to check. Omit to check every column except grouping keys.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping variables. Grouped data use their groups unless .by is supplied.

.patterns

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, tabulate missing patterns instead of counting by variable.

.all

A single TRUE or FALSE. If FALSE (default), only variables with at least one missing value are shown, as in Stata; if TRUE, all checked variables are shown.

Value

By default, a tibble with any grouping keys, variable, miss_n (missing values), miss_pct (percentage of rows, from zero to 100) and valid_n (observed values), one row per variable (and group).

With .patterns = TRUE, a tibble with any grouping keys, one column per variable holding 1 (observed) or 0 (missing) as in Stata, n (rows with that pattern) and percent (of the rows in the group). Patterns are sorted by decreasing frequency within each group, so the first row is usually the complete cases.

Details

A value is missing when is.na() is TRUE for it, which includes NaN and haven's tagged missing values such as Stata's .a. Empty strings are observed values, unlike Stata's missing string; convert them first with na_if_value(). When no checked variable has missing values and .all = FALSE, a message says so and the result has no variable rows or columns.

See also

Other inspection functions: browse(), codebook(), names, var_type(), variables()

Examples

misstable(lifeexp)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   variable  miss_n miss_pct valid_n
#>   <chr>      <int>    <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 gnppc          1     1.47      67
#> 2 safewater     14    20.6       54
misstable(lifeexp, .all = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   variable  miss_n miss_pct valid_n
#>   <chr>      <int>    <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 region         0     0         68
#> 2 country        0     0         68
#> 3 popgrowth      0     0         68
#> 4 lexp           0     0         68
#> 5 gnppc          1     1.47      67
#> 6 safewater     14    20.6       54
misstable(lifeexp, .patterns = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   gnppc safewater     n percent
#>   <int>     <int> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1     1         1    53   77.9 
#> 2     1         0    14   20.6 
#> 3     0         1     1    1.47
misstable(lifeexp, gnppc, safewater, .by = region)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   region               variable  miss_n miss_pct valid_n
#>   <dbl+lbl>            <chr>      <int>    <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] gnppc          1     2.27      43
#> 2 1 [Europe & C. Asia] safewater      2     4.55      42
#> 3 2 [North America]    gnppc          0     0         14
#> 4 2 [North America]    safewater      8    57.1        6
#> 5 3 [South America]    gnppc          0     0         10
#> 6 3 [South America]    safewater      4    40          6
misstable(dplyr::starwars, height, mass, birth_year, .patterns = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   height  mass birth_year     n percent
#>    <int> <int>      <int> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1      1     1          1    36   41.4 
#> 2      1     1          0    23   26.4 
#> 3      1     0          0    15   17.2 
#> 4      1     0          1     7    8.05
#> 5      0     0          0     6    6.90
